summary: Defines two MIB modules used by other MIB modules for monitoring or configuring Layer 2 and Layer 3 VPNs that support multicast.

eli5.summary: This is a set of dials and gauges for watching shared multicast on private networks.

questions: what is the l2l3 vpn multicast mib
what is a pmsi tunnel attribute
what is a p-tunnel in multicast vpn
what is the difference between i-pmsi and s-pmsi
subtitle: Two MIB modules that describe the provider tunnels used to carry multicast in BGP/MPLS Layer 2 and Layer 3 VPNs.

tldr.problem: Management modules for multicast VPNs all need a common way to name and look up the provider tunnels that carry customer multicast traffic.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two textual conventions (tunnel type and tunnel identifier) and a table with one row per provider tunnel on a PE router, indexed by type and identifier.
tldr.outcome: Other MIB modules can reuse these definitions to monitor or configure multicast VPNs. All objects are read-only or not-accessible.

today: RFC 8502 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Multicast VPNs and Provider Tunnels
sections.content:
In BGP/MPLS Virtual Private Networks, BGP distributes routes and MPLS forwards packets across the service provider network. Multicast support is specified in RFC 6513 for Layer 3 VPNs and RFC 7117 for Layer 2 VPNs. The RFC calls a BGP/MPLS L2 or L3 VPN that supports multicast an L2L3VpnMCast network.

Such networks forward a packet to all or some Provider Edge (PE) routers through provider tunnels (P-tunnels). The tunnel type says which technology builds the tunnel, and the type plus the identifier together identify one tunnel. A PMSI Tunnel attribute, carried in BGP auto-discovery routes and defined in RFC 6514, holds this information.

This document supplies textual conventions and managed objects that other MIB modules can use. It adopts the definitions of RFC 6513, RFC 6514 and RFC 7117 and assumes the reader knows multicast, MPLS and VPN concepts.
sections.eli5: A company has several offices that share a private network. Provider tunnels are the hidden pipes that carry a video call to all offices at once. This RFC gives each pipe a label so tools can list them.

sections.title: PMSI, I-PMSI and S-PMSI
sections.content:
A PMSI (Provider Multicast Service Interface) is a conceptual interface instantiated by a P-tunnel. A PE uses it to send customer multicast traffic to all or some PEs in the same VPN.

An I-PMSI (Inclusive) lets a PE send to all PEs in the same VPN. An S-PMSI (Selective) lets it send to only some of them. The document uses the single term PMSI for both.
sections.eli5: An inclusive tunnel is like a loudspeaker that reaches every office. A selective one is like a phone call to only a few of them.

sections.title: The Two MIB Modules
sections.content:
The Internet-Standard Management Framework lets managed objects be read through SNMP, with objects defined in SMIv2 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579, RFC 2580).

L2L3-VPN-MULTICAST-TC-MIB holds two textual conventions, L2L3VpnMcastProviderTunnelType and L2L3VpnMcastProviderTunnelId. L2L3-VPN-MULTICAST-MIB defines one table, l2L3VpnMcastPmsiTunnelAttributeTable. Each row describes a specific P-tunnel on a PE router, and the index (type plus identifier) uniquely identifies the tunnel.

The table can be combined with the MPLS-TE-STD-MIB (RFC 3812) for more detail on a tunnel, or with the Interfaces Group MIB (RFC 2863) for the interface that corresponds to it.
sections.eli5: One module is the list of allowed name tags. The other is a table where each row describes one tunnel, using those tags.

sections.title: Tunnel Types and Identifiers
sections.content:
The tunnel type is an enumeration aligned with the tunnel types registered for BGP: noTunnelInfo (0), rsvpP2mp (1), ldpP2mp (2), pimSsm (3), pimAsm (4), pimBidir (5), ingressReplication (6), ldpMp2mp (7) and transportTunnel (8).

The tunnel identifier is an octet string whose size depends on the type and on whether IPv4 or IPv6 is used. For example, a PIM tree uses source plus group address (8 octets in IPv4, 32 in IPv6), ingress replication uses the local PE's unicast endpoint address (4 or 16 octets), and mLDP uses a FEC element (17 or 29 octets). With noTunnelInfo the identifier is a zero-length string.
sections.eli5: There are nine kinds of tunnel, numbered 0 to 8. Each kind has its own style of name tag, and the tag is longer when addresses are longer.

sections.title: The PMSI Tunnel Attribute Table
sections.content:
The table is indexed by l2L3VpnMcastPmsiTunnelAttributeType and l2L3VpnMcastPmsiTunnelAttributeId, which mirror the Tunnel Type and Tunnel Identifier fields of the PMSI Tunnel attribute. Both are not-accessible index objects.

Four read-only columns follow. l2L3VpnMCastPmsiTunnelLeafInfoRequired reports whether the originating PE asked receivers to originate a Leaf A-D route (false 0, true 1, notAvailable 2). l2L3VpnMcastPmsiTunnelAttributeMplsLabel gives the MPLS label in the attribute, or zero if there is no attribute. l2L3VpnMcastPmsiTunnelPointer points to a row in another table such as mplsTunnelTable, and l2L3VpnMcastPmsiTunnelIf points to a row in ifXTable. Each pointer is zeroDotZero if no such row exists.

Conformance: the core group (leaf information and MPLS label) is required, and the optional group (the two pointers) is optional.
sections.eli5: For each tunnel the table records a few facts: does it ask for replies, what label does it use, and where can I find more about it.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
No object has a MAX-ACCESS of read-write or read-create, so correct implementations cannot be altered through SNMP SET. The RFC still says the tunnel table can reveal the P-tunnel topology, for example source and group addresses in the identifier, so GET and notification access may need control and, in some environments, encryption.

Implementations SHOULD provide the SNMPv3 security features, and deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED. IANA assigned { mib-2 244 } to the TC module and { mib-2 245 } to the main module.
sections.eli5: Nobody can change these gauges, but the readings show how the private pipes are laid out, so only trusted people should be allowed to look.
